bibl.title: Older Adults Perceptions of Technology and Barriers to Interacting with Tablet Computers: A Focus Group Study

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: what eighteen older adults with no tablet experience say about tablets and technology, in three focus groups
span.quote: Eighteen older adults (65–76 years old; 83.3% female) who were novice tablet users participated in discussions about their perceptions of and barriers to interacting with tablets.

span.label: what older adults perceive as the advantages, disadvantages and barriers of interacting with tablets
span.quote: The themes that emerged were related to barriers (i.e., lack of instructions and guidance, lack of knowledge and confidence, health-related barriers, cost); disadvantages and concerns (i.e., too much and too complex technology, feelings of inadequacy, and comparison with younger generations, lack of social interaction and communication, negative features of tablets); advantages (i.e., positive features of tablets, accessing information, willingness to adopt technology); and skepticism about using tablets and technology in general.

span.label: a thematic account in which eagerness to adopt coexists with low confidence, and instruction rather than motivation is the reported obstacle
span.quote: Our findings suggest that most of our participants were eager to adopt new technology and willing to learn using a tablet. However, they voiced apprehension about lack of, or lack of clarity in, instructions and support.

span.label: existence
span.quote: The themes that emerged were related to barriers (i.e., lack of instructions and guidance, lack of knowledge and confidence, health-related barriers, cost); disadvantages and concerns (i.e., too much and too complex technology, feelings of inadequacy, and comparison with younger generations, lack of social interaction and communication, negative features of tablets); advantages (i.e., positive features of tablets, accessing information, willingness to adopt technology); and skepticism about using tablets and technology in general.

span.label: slower adoption of new technology by older adults
span.quote: The theory of diffusion of innovations (Rogers, 2010 ) also holds that older adults are less likely to adopt new technologies unless they view clear benefits of using them.

span.label: three focus groups, generic qualitative design, thematic analysis, snowball recruitment
span.term: three focus groups, generic qualitative design, thematic analysis, snowball recruitment
span.quote: We conducted three separate focus groups and used a generic qualitative design applying thematic analysis to analyse the data.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: BENEFIT OUTWEIGHS COST RATHER THAN COST DETERRING: technology acceptance in older adults tracks the perceived benefit more than the perceived price, which the paper reads through diffusion of innovations - adoption follows a clear benefit being visible
span.quote: This finding is consistent with previous studies suggesting the perception of potential benefits was more indicative of technology acceptance than perception of cost

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: EAGERNESS AND LOW CONFIDENCE COEXIST: most participants wanted to adopt the technology and the majority simultaneously doubted their own ability to use it, so the obstacle reported is instruction rather than motivation
span.quote: Our findings suggest that most of our participants were eager to adopt new technology and willing to learn using a tablet. However, they voiced apprehension about lack of, or lack of clarity in, instructions and support.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A CATEGORY CONFUSION UNDERNEATH THE BARRIERS: participants were unaware of the differences between device types, so 'technology' is being evaluated as one undifferentiated thing
span.quote: questions that they were unaware of the similarities and differences between different types of technology (e.g., laptop vs. tablet).

span.label: The sample is small and the paper says larger studies are needed before the findings generalise
span.quote: Finally, our sample was small and therefore larger studies are needed to be able to generalize these findings to populations.

span.label: RESPONSE BIAS IN A FOCUS GROUP IS NAMED BY THE AUTHORS: the enthusiasm reported should be read with caution because of the setting in which it was expressed
span.quote: Finally, although the participants enjoyed the tablet experience and emphasized the likelihood of using a tablet in the future, these results should be interpreted with caution given the possible response bias of participants in the focus group setting.

span.label: SELECTION BIAS WAS NOT ACTIVELY PREVENTED - stated in those words - and is argued against afterwards from the data rather than designed out
span.quote: While selection bias was not actively prevented, one third of the participants reported that they were undecided or unlikely to use a tablet in the future, suggesting that it was not only people who were interested in using tablets participated.

span.label: Participants were naive tablet users by design, so the findings do not speak for experienced users
span.quote: The focus of the current study was on naïve participants, as in the proposed tablet intervention, participants will be using tablet technology for the first time.

span.label: Recruitment was by snowball sampling in one city, which the paper reports and does not treat as a limitation
span.quote: Potential participants were recruited from the Edinburgh area by contacting clubs for older adults, community centers and email lists using the snowball principle (Goodman, 1961 ).

span.label: one third of participants reported being undecided or unlikely to use a tablet in future, offered as evidence that the sample was not only enthusiasts
span.note: eliminates: selection bias toward people already interested in tablets
span.quote: While selection bias was not actively prevented, one third of the participants reported that they were undecided or unlikely to use a tablet in the future, suggesting that it was not only people who were interested in using tablets participated.

span.label: cost - A BARRIER ONLY FOR THE EXPERIENCED. The paper notices that only participants with prior computer experience raised it, and offers the reading that inexperience means not knowing what the devices cost
span.quote: Interestingly, only participants with previous computer experience brought up the latter in our study. It is possible that cost is not one of the main barriers to using technology for people with less experience; their lack of exposure to technology in general may mean they are less aware of the costs of such devices, or simply that other concerns take priority.
